label: Discord
terms_note: Bot accounts in guilds the bot was invited to. Global 50 requests / second per bot; per-route buckets (X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset-After / -Bucket / -Scope), 429 with retry_after; 10,000 invalid requests (401 / 403 / 429) per 10 minutes → temporary Cloudflare ban. Privileged intents GUILD_PRESENCES, GUILD_MEMBERS, MESSAGE_CONTENT need review once the app is in 100+ servers / 10,000+ unique users; message content is always available for the bot's own messages, DMs with the bot, messages mentioning it, and context-menu targets. DMs: POST /users/@me/channels {recipient_id} — 'you should not use this endpoint to DM everyone in a server about something'; DMs must stem from user actions, mass DMs → rate limiting or bot removal; group DMs need OAuth2 gdm.join (effectively unavailable). Threads: from a message (PUBLIC_THREAD), without message (PRIVATE_THREAD in GUILD_TEXT), forum / media posts via POST /channels/{id}/threads with a message; auto_archive_duration 60 / 1440 / 4320 / 10080 min; channel rate_limit_per_user 0-21,600 s.

sdks: Community libraries (discord.js, discord.py, JDA, …); REST is plain HTTPS with Authorization: Bot (docs.discord.com)

tools.name: mark_read
tools.endpoint: — (read state is a user-token/client concept, not a bot one)

endpoints.notes: content needs `MESSAGE_CONTENT` except own messages, DMs with the bot, mentions, context-menu targets

endpoints.call: POST /channels/{id}/messages/{id}/threads` (PUBLIC_THREAD) · `POST /channels/{id}/threads` (PRIVATE_THREAD in GUILD_TEXT; forum / media posts with `message`)

endpoints.notes: only users sharing a guild who allow DMs; "you should not use this endpoint to DM everyone in a server" — user-initiated only, mass DMs → rate limit / removal

reference.limits: - Global **50 requests / second per bot**; per-route buckets via `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset-After` / `-Bucket` / `-Scope`; 429 → `retry_after`; **10,000 invalid requests (401 / 403 / 429) per 10 minutes → temporary IP ban**. - Group DMs need OAuth2 `gdm.join` (legacy GameBridge) — effectively unavailable. Developer Terms / Policy forbid unsolicited mass DMs.

fields.name: bot_token
fields.help: Bot token from the app's Bot page in the Developer Portal, pasted WITHOUT the 'Bot ' prefix: the runtime adds it and sends 'Authorization: Bot <token>' ('authentication is performed with the Authorization HTTP header in the format Authorization: TOKEN_TYPE TOKEN', https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#authentication). Channel permissions needed: VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY (list_inbound, get_thread), SEND_MESSAGES (send, reply); the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent to read other users' message content.

adapter.rate_note: 'All bots can make up to 50 requests per second to our API' globally, plus per-route buckets announced in X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset / -Reset-After / -Bucket and enforced with 429 + Retry-After (https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits). Per-route numbers are not published, so the client bucket stays at the runtime default 2/s.
adapter.user_agent_note: Discord asks HTTP clients for a User-Agent 'in the following format: DiscordBot ($url, $versionNumber)' (https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#user-agent); the runtime sends its own 'platform-mcp/discord (+url)' User-Agent, which is a valid but non-canonical value (UNCONFIRMED whether Discord ever rejects it).

me.note: 'Returns the user object of the requester's account' — for a bot token the bot's own user (id, username, discriminator, global_name, bot: true).

send.note: `to` is a CHANNEL id (snowflake), not a user or address: 'Post a message to a guild text or DM channel' — to reach a user, first open a DM channel with POST /users/@me/channels (not offered) and pass that channel id. `text` is `content`, 'Message contents (up to 2000 characters)'; `subject` and `channel` are ignored. Needs SEND_MESSAGES in the channel. message_id is the created message's id.

reply.note: A Discord reply is a message carrying a message_reference to the parent: 'Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message. When sending, only message_id is required'. `thread_id` is that parent message id and `channel` (the channel the parent lives in) is REQUIRED — without it the runtime reports missing argument 'channel'. Needs READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY as well as SEND_MESSAGES ('The referenced message must exist and cannot be a system message').

list_inbound.note: Lists ONE channel: `channel` (a channel or thread id) is REQUIRED — bots have no cross-channel inbox endpoint (inbound push is the Gateway). 'Returns an array of message objects from newest to oldest'; Discord pages by message id (before / after / around), so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` (1-100, Discord default 50) messages are returned; `since` is not sent. 'If the current user is missing the READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY permission in the channel, then no messages will be returned', and other users' `content` is empty without the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. `from` is author.id (username under raw.author); `thread_id` is the channel id; `sent_at` is the ISO-8601 `timestamp`.

get_thread.note: A Discord thread is itself a channel, so `thread_id` is the thread's channel id (a message's `thread.id`, or the id from a THREAD_CREATE event) and the same Get Channel Messages endpoint lists it; the vocabulary's `channel` is ignored. Same newest-first / id-cursor caveats as list_inbound (`page` ignored, newest `limit` messages only).

not_offered.mark_read: Read state is a user-client concept; the bot-facing Channel and Message resources document no endpoint that marks a channel or message as read (https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel, https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message).
